correctness.rationale: The exact t-deletion intersection criterion follows from matching rm-t symbols: at most t original blocks contain a source deletion, and at most t additional blocks straddle a receiver deletion, so r>=2t+1 forces a whole consecutive block to align. The signed index displacement is at most t, and conversely a signed cyclic shift of size <=t supplies a length rm-t common subsequence. Therefore components are precisely cycle powers on the rotation classes, of cardinality their least periods d. Cyclic gaps >=t+1 show independent-set maximum k_d; marked-origin gap compositions count all optimum subsets h_d; Möbius inversion counts primitive classes. For fixed q,t, primitive length-m words dominate to give rate 1/(t+1). Actual Python checker independently forms all deletion sets for 16 parameter triples and all codebooks for universes <=16, with no counterexamples. Finite tests are not substituted for the all-parameter proof.

value.rationale: Repeated message blocks are a natural synchronization code under adversarial deletion. The theorem proves a structural obstruction: cyclic phase shifts of at most t remain confusable regardless of additional whole-message copies, and gives exact optimal payload capacity and the complete number of optimal q-ary subcodes for every block length. In particular, the limiting retained-message fraction is a sharp 1/(t+1). This is a natural all-length family classification rather than a routine single numeric evaluation or a restatement of primitive-necklace enumeration.
